A 12-day-old baby has died after an avocado fell from a tree in Argentina. His mother alleges the local council ignored repeated warnings about the danger.


## Newborn Baby Dies After Falling Avocado Strikes His Head


A tragic incident in Argentina has left a family devastated after a newborn baby died from injuries sustained when an avocado reportedly fell from a tree and struck his head. The child's mother has accused local authorities of failing to act on repeated requests to address concerns about trees near a nursery.


Lucas, who was just 12 days old, was being held by his mother, Guiliana Gomez, outside a nursery in Quilmes, Buenos Aires Province, when the incident occurred on Thursday, 22 October 2026, according to reports cited by *The Independent* .


The baby was with his mother as she dropped off her five-year-old son at the educational facility on Calle Conesa. During the visit, an avocado reportedly fell from a nearby tree and struck the newborn on the head, causing severe injuries.


The incident has raised concerns about public safety, tree maintenance and whether warnings about potential hazards near schools and nurseries were adequately addressed.


## Baby Suffered Severe Head Injuries


According to media reports, the falling fruit caused multiple skull fractures, leaving Lucas in critical condition.


A witness quoted by Argentine publication *El Día* described the moments following the incident, explaining that the baby initially showed no visible bleeding before beginning to cry.


The witness reportedly helped hold the infant as his mother reacted to what had happened.


Emergency assistance was called, although a witness alleged that the ambulance arrived approximately 20 minutes later and did not have the appropriate equipment to treat the baby.


Lucas was subsequently taken for medical treatment. He reportedly underwent around three hours of surgery before being transferred to intensive care.


Despite medical efforts to save him, the newborn died four days later, on Sunday, 25 October 2026.


His death has prompted renewed scrutiny of the circumstances surrounding the incident and the safety of the area where it occurred.


## Mother Claims Council Ignored Repeated Warnings


Following her son's death, Gomez accused the local municipality of failing to respond to concerns about trees growing close to the nursery.


She alleged that residents and school representatives had repeatedly requested pruning or removal of three trees in the area for more than a year.


According to her account, the requests dated back to 2025, when concerns were reportedly raised about falling avocados near the entrance and exit of the educational facility.


The mother believes the tragedy could potentially have been prevented if the trees had been inspected or maintained earlier.


Her allegations have placed the spotlight on the responsibility of local authorities to assess and manage hazards in public spaces, particularly in areas regularly visited by young children and their families.


However, the allegations have not yet been established as findings of legal responsibility. The ongoing investigation will be important in determining the circumstances of the death and whether any official failures occurred.


## Previous Incidents Reportedly Raised Safety Concerns


The family has also claimed that the danger associated with the trees was not entirely unexpected.


According to statements attributed to Lucas's uncle and reported by *El Día* , school records contained requests for the municipality to remove the tree dating back to the previous year.


The uncle also alleged that a father had previously been knocked unconscious by a falling avocado and that other children had narrowly avoided being struck.


These claims raise questions about whether earlier incidents were reported to the relevant authorities and what action, if any, followed.


The family further alleged that the tree was cut down after Lucas's death.


If verified, the timing of the removal could become relevant to questions about how officials responded to earlier complaints. However, the available reports do not establish the full history of the requests, the municipality's response before the incident, or the reasons for the subsequent removal.


A complete account will depend on the evidence gathered by investigators and any official records released during the inquiry.


## Family Demands Accountability After Newborn's Death


Gomez has expressed deep frustration over the response she received following her son's death.


She claimed that the municipality arranged contact with a psychologist who asked about Lucas's condition after he had already died. She also said that no other representatives had contacted her.


The mother has called for those responsible to be held accountable.


Her comments reflect the distress of a family dealing with the sudden loss of a newborn while seeking answers about whether the incident could have been prevented.


In a letter to her son shared by Argentine publication *Revista Gente* , Gomez expressed her love and grief, remembering the brief time they had together.


She described Lucas as a fighter and reflected on the happiness he brought to the family during his short life.


She also referred to the need to remain strong for his siblings, while emphasising that her son would always remain in her heart and memories.


The letter has brought further attention to the family's loss and the emotional impact of the tragedy.


## Investigation Into the Baby's Death Underway


The Quilmes Prosecutor's Office No. 9 is investigating the circumstances surrounding Lucas's death, according to reports cited by Argentine newspaper *La Nación* .


The case was initially classified as a death involving alleged negligent injury, as described in the reporting.


That initial classification should not be interpreted as a final legal finding. Investigators will need to establish the precise circumstances of the incident and assess any evidence relevant to possible negligence.


Key questions include whether complaints about the tree were formally submitted, whether the municipality received and processed those requests, and whether the tree presented a foreseeable risk to people using the area.


Investigators may also need to examine the sequence of events on the day of the incident and the actions taken after the baby was injured.


The outcome of the investigation could help clarify whether any individuals or public bodies bear legal responsibility.


Until further findings are released, allegations made by the family should remain clearly distinguished from facts established by the authorities.


## Why Tree Maintenance and Public Safety Matter


The tragedy has highlighted broader questions about the maintenance of trees in public areas, particularly around schools, nurseries and other places where children gather.


Trees provide shade, support local ecosystems and improve neighbourhood environments. However, falling branches, fruit and other objects can sometimes present safety concerns, depending on the species, tree condition, height and surrounding environment.


Regular inspections and appropriate maintenance can help identify potential hazards before they cause injuries.


Where residents, parents or school representatives report a possible danger, clear reporting procedures and timely assessments are important. Authorities also need effective systems for documenting complaints, prioritising risks and communicating decisions to those affected.


The incident in Quilmes demonstrates why allegations of unresolved safety concerns deserve careful investigation. It also illustrates the importance of establishing what was known before an accident occurred, rather than drawing conclusions based solely on events that followed.


Whether earlier action would have prevented Lucas's death remains a matter for investigators to assess.


## Conclusion


The death of 12-day-old Lucas after he was reportedly struck by a falling avocado in Quilmes, Argentina, has devastated his family and prompted serious questions about public safety.


His mother, Guiliana Gomez, alleges that repeated requests to prune or remove trees near a nursery were ignored before the incident. Family members have also described previous accidents and near misses involving falling fruit.


Authorities are investigating the circumstances of the newborn's death, and the allegations of negligence have yet to be established through a final legal finding.


As the inquiry continues, the family is seeking answers and accountability for a loss that has profoundly affected their lives.


The case serves as a reminder of the importance of taking reported hazards seriously, maintaining public spaces responsibly and ensuring that safety concerns receive appropriate attention.


**Source:** *The Independent* on 29 October 2026.
